'''Jean-Pierre Gattuso''' ({{IPA|fr|ʒɑ̃ pjɛʁ gatɥzo}}) (born 14 December 1958 in [[Antibes]]) is a French ocean scientist conducting research globally, from the pole to the tropics and from nearshore to the open ocean. His research addresses the biology of reef-building corals, the biogeochemistry of coastal ecosystems, and the response of marine plants, animals and ecosystems to global environmental change. He is also interested in transdisciplinary research, collaborating with social scientists to address ocean-based solutions to minimize climate change and its impacts. He is currently a [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] Research Professor at [[Sorbonne University]].

==Education==
Gattuso earned a bachelor's degree from the [[University of Nice]] (1980) and a master's degree in oceanography at the [[University of Aix-Marseille II]]. In 1987, he obtained a Ph.D. in oceanography from the [[University of Aix-Marseille II]].<ref name="phd">{{Cite thesis |title= PhD|date=January 1987 |publisher=Aix-Marseille 2 |url=https://www.theses.fr/1987AIX22054|type=These de doctorat |last1=Gattuso |first1=Jean-Pierre }}</ref>

==Career==
Upon receiving his Ph.D., Gattuso moved to Australia where he was a [[postdoctoral researcher]] at the [[Australian Institute of Marine Science]](1988-1990). In 1990, Gattuso took a position of [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] research scientist at Centre de Biologie et Écologie Tropicale et Méditerranéenne of the [[University of Perpignan]] (1990-1992). He then moved to the Scientific Center of Monaco to launch and lead the [[Ecophysiology]] and Biogeochemistry group. In 1998, Gattuso went back to a CNRS joint laboratory at the [[Observatoire Oceanologique de Villefranche|Villefranche Oceanographic Observatory]] and moved to the ranks of Research Professor (directeur de recherche). He is also Associate Scientist at the Institute for Sustainable Development and International Relations (IDDRI-SciencesPo, Paris).<ref name="iddri">{{Cite web |title= IDDRI|url=https://www.iddri.org/en}}</ref> Gattuso has been visiting professor or scientist at [[Rutgers University]], the [[National Center for Atmospheric Research]] and [[Shantou University]].

Gattuso is the founding editor-in-chief of Biogeosciences <ref>{{Cite web |title=Biogeosciences |url=https://www.biogeosciences.net}}</ref> and served or has served in the editorial board of several scientific journals. He founded the Biogeosciences Division <ref>{{Cite web |title= Biogeosciences Division |url=https://www.egu.eu/bg/home/}}</ref> of the [[European Geosciences Union]], and has received multiple awards and honors for his research contributions. He led the launch of the Ocean Acidification International Coordination Centre <ref>{{Cite web |title=Ocean Acidification International Coordination Centre|date=5 February 2018 |url=https://www.iaea.org/services/oa-icc}}</ref> at the International Atomic Energy Agency, co-edited the first book on ocean acidification <ref name="livre">{{Cite book |title=Ocean Acidification | date=15 September 2011 | publisher=Oxford University Press | isbn=978-0-19-959109-1 |url=https://global.oup.com/academic/product/ocean-acidification-9780199591091?cc=fr&lang=en&}}</ref> (Oxford University Press) and contributed to several IPCC products ([[IPCC Fifth Assessment Report|5th Assessment Report]], [[Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 °C|Special Report on 1.5°C of Warming]], and the [[Special Report on the Ocean and Cryosphere in a Changing Climate]]).

Gattuso co-chaired the One Ocean Science Congress,<ref>{{Cite web |title=One Ocean Science Congress|url=https://one-ocean-science-2025.org/}}</ref> a [[United Nations]] special event which preceded the [[2025 United Nations Ocean Conference]].

==Research==
Gattuso was originally trained as a marine biologist. He first investigated photoadaptation of reef-building corals.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gattuso |first1=J.-P. |last2=Jaubert |first2=J.|title=Computation of metabolic quotients in plant-animal symbiotic units |journal=Journal of Theoretical Biology |date=1988 |volume=130 |issue=2 |pages=205–212 |doi=10.1016/S0022-5193(88)80095-X |bibcode=1988JThBi.130..205G }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gattuso |first1=J.-P. |last2=Allemand |first2=D.|last3=Frankignoulle |first3=M.|title=Photosynthesis and calcification at cellular, organismal and community levels in coral reefs: a review on interactions and control by carbonate chemistry.|journal=American Zoologist |date=1999 |volume=39 |issue=1|pages=160–183 |doi=10.1093/icb/39.1.160 |jstor=3884234 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
He then looked at the cycling of carbon and carbonates in corals and coral reefs.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Gattuso |first1=J.-P. |last2=Pichon |first2=M.|last3=Delesalle |first3=B.|last4=Frankignoulle |first4=M.|title=Community metabolism and air-sea CO2 fluxes in a coral reef ecosystem (Moorea, French Polynesia).|journal=Marine Ecology Progress Series|date=1993 |volume=96 |issue=3|pages=259–267 |doi=10.3354/meps096259 |bibcode=1993MEPS...96..259G |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/i24833547|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Gattuso |first1=J.-P. |last2=Frankignoulle |first2=M.|last3=Smith |first3=S.V.|title=Measurement of community metabolism and significance of coral reefs in the CO2 source-sink debate.|journal= Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|date=1999 |volume=96 |issue=23|pages=13017–13022|doi=10.1073/pnas.96.23.13017|pmid=10557265 |pmc=23892 |doi-access=free}}</ref> These biogeochemical studies were expanded * 2025: Chevalier, Ordre national de la Légion d'honneur <ref>{{Cite web |title=Décret du 11 juillet 2025 portant promotion et nomination dans l'ordre national de la Légion d'honneur|url=https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/download/pdf?id=9zISAJoUW7vqqFowMZPozN_gRqcUA3qn9Cpuf_2cwJA=}}</ref>
* 2025: Engaged for the ocean award of Fondation de la mer <ref>{{Cite web |title=Jean-Pierre Gattuso, lauréat 2025 catégorie scientifique|date=April 2025 |url=https://www.fondationdelamer.org/nos-actualites/jean-pierre-gattuso-laureat-2025/}}</ref>
* 2024: Fellow, [[Association for the Sciences of Limnology and Oceanography]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=ASLO Fellows 2024|url=https://www.aslo.org/aslo-fellows-2024//}}</ref>
* 2023, Elected foreign member,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Foreign member elected at the Chinese Academy of Sciences in 2023|url=http://www.casad.cas.cn/yszx/yszx2023/tzgg/202311/t20231122_4986750.html|access-date=2023-12-27|archive-date=2023-11-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231123103522/http://www.casad.cas.cn/yszx/yszx2023/tzgg/202311/t20231122_4986750.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]

* 2014, Blaise Pascal Medal in Earth and Environmental Sciences,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Blaise Pascal Medal in Earth and Environmental Sciences E|url=https://www.eurasc.org/eurasc-awardees/blaise-pascal-medals}}</ref> and elected member of the European Academy of Sciences
* 2012, Vladimir Vernadsky Medal,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Vladimir Vernadsky Medal|url=https://www.egu.eu/awards-medals/vladimir-ivanovich-vernadsky/2012/jean-pierre-gattuso/}}</ref> [[European Geosciences Union]]
